block, labs false.description:
Drive the user's Cloud workspaces in Arugula control, as the user (the owner of this machine): make one, open a tab (an agent on its machine), prompt it and wait for its turn, interrupt it, answer what it asks, close it, rebuild or retry. The user sees it all on control's page. Changing a Cloud workspace's settings or deleting one is theirs, on that page. A hosted Cloud workspace (hw_…, made with project) is a machine of the project: its tabs are agent blocks on it (claude or codex), by pane number, which the project's people see too; the machine tools reach it with cloud_workspace.
- create {name, apt?, env_vars?, npm?, project?, repositories?, secrets?, setup_script?}: A new Cloud workspace: a machine with these repositories checked out, packages installed and setup script run. It sets up for a few minutes (list kind cloud_workspaces says its step; read_cloud kind setup_log what it printed); a tab opened meanwhile starts once it's ready. Returns its id.
- open_tab {cloud_workspace, agent?, cwd?, model?, prompt?}: A new tab in a Cloud workspace: an agent's conversation on its machine, with a first prompt if given. Returns the tab's id; wait with the tab until idle or needs_input.
- prompt {cloud_workspace, tab, text, timeout?}: Give a tab's agent a prompt and wait for its turn: returns when it ends (done, with the reply), when it asks for someone (needs_input, with its requests: answer one), or still running after timeout, with the offset to wait after. A parked machine wakes for it; a tab whose conversation failed starts a new one with it.
- interrupt {cloud_workspace, tab}: Stop the turn a tab's agent is in. The tab stays open.
- answer {cloud_workspace, request, tab, action?, content?, option?}: Answer what a tab's agent asks (read_cloud kind requests): a permission request with option, a question with action (and content, its fields, to accept).
- close_tab {cloud_workspace, tab}: Close a tab: its conversation and agent end; its transcript is kept. The other tabs and the machine carry on.
- rebuild {cloud_workspace, interrupt?}: Replace a Cloud workspace's machine with one set up from its settings as saved: its disk is wiped; its tabs keep their conversations. Refused while a tab's turn runs, unless interrupt.
- retry {cloud_workspace}: Set up a Cloud workspace whose setup failed again (read_cloud kind setup_log says why it failed).

block, labs true.description:
Build a Doc, a report, plan or write-up longer than a screen, in a block beside your pane that the user (and anyone the session is shared with) watches fill in. Make the outline first with new, so they see every section at once; then fill each section in order and say one sentence about it in the pane. Never write the Doc's files by hand.
- new {sections, title, beside?}: A Doc: a block beside your pane that holds a report, plan or write-up, with its outline (every section's heading and intent) shown at once. Returns the block and the section ids (s1, s2, …); fill them next, in order.
- fill {block, markdown, section}: Write one section of a Doc (its block, the section id, its Markdown): headings, paragraphs, lists, **bold**, *italic*, `code`, links and tables. No HTML. A picture is ![alt](assets/<name>) after doc asset has put it there. A section is at most 64 KB, a Doc 40 sections and 1 MiB; filling a section again replaces it.

Two kinds of fenced block draw as more than code, in the section that talks about them.
A chart: a ```chart fence holding a JSON spec. type is "bar" or "line"; title is optional; x is the key of each row that labels it; y is a key, or a list of up to 4 keys, whose values are numbers (not strings); rows is 1 to 200 objects. A line chart's x must go up: numbers, ISO dates (2026-01-31), or labels listed in order with "order": [...]. For example:
```chart
{"type": "bar", "title": "Sales by month", "x": "month", "y": ["sales"], "rows": [{"month": "Jan", "sales": 12}, {"month": "Feb", "sales": 19}]}
```
A drawing: a ```svg fence holding one <svg> element, with xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" on it and a viewBox. Any text after svg on the fence line is its alt text. It is shown as a picture, so scripts in it don't run. For example:
```svg Idea to app
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 160 40"><rect x="2" y="8" width="60" height="24" fill="#e8f0fe" stroke="#335"/><path d="M62 20 H98" stroke="#335"/><rect x="98" y="8" width="60" height="24" fill="#e6f4ea" stroke="#335"/></svg>
```
Every fence is checked before anything is written: a bad chart or drawing is refused with one line saying what to fix, and the section stays as it was.
- asset {block, name, data?, path?}: Put a picture in a Doc (its block, a name, and one of path or data): a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, at most 2 MB, at most 20 per Doc. path is an absolute path to a file you saved; an agent on a machine of its own sends data (base64) instead. What the bytes are decides the type, so the name has to end in the right extension (.png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif, .webp); an SVG file is refused: draw it with a ```svg fence. Returns assets/<name>; show it in a section with ![what it shows](assets/<name>). Put the asset before the doc fill that names it: a fill naming an asset the Doc doesn't have is refused. Only assets/ images show; an http:// or ../ one is refused. A name already used is replaced. For example: {"kind": "asset", "block": 7, "name": "flow.png", "path": "/tmp/flow.png"}.
- share {block}: Ask the user to share a finished Doc (its block) with a link anyone can open, without an account. A card asks them on the Doc and nothing is published until they tap Share; this returns {status: "waiting"} at once. Call share again on the same block to learn the outcome: shared (with the url, which you can give the user), declined, lapsed (a card nobody answered in a day) or failed (with why). A Doc already shared answers shared. Asking again after a decline raises a new card. Don't ask more than once for a Doc unless the user wants it.

block, labs true.description:
Drive the user's Cloud workspaces in Arugula control, as the user (the owner of this machine): make one, open a tab (an agent on its machine), prompt it and wait for its turn, interrupt it, answer what it asks, close it, rebuild or retry. The user sees it all on control's page. Changing a Cloud workspace's settings or deleting one is theirs, on that page. A hosted Cloud workspace (hw_…, made with project) is a machine of the project: its tabs are agent blocks on it (claude or codex), by pane number, which the project's people see too; the machine tools reach it with cloud_workspace.
- create {name, apt?, env_vars?, npm?, project?, repositories?, secrets?, setup_script?}: A new Cloud workspace: a machine with these repositories checked out, packages installed and setup script run. It sets up for a few minutes (list kind cloud_workspaces says its step; read_cloud kind setup_log what it printed); a tab opened meanwhile starts once it's ready. Returns its id.
- open_tab {cloud_workspace, agent?, cwd?, model?, prompt?}: A new tab in a Cloud workspace: an agent's conversation on its machine, with a first prompt if given. Returns the tab's id; wait with the tab until idle or needs_input.
- prompt {cloud_workspace, tab, text, timeout?}: Give a tab's agent a prompt and wait for its turn: returns when it ends (done, with the reply), when it asks for someone (needs_input, with its requests: answer one), or still running after timeout, with the offset to wait after. A parked machine wakes for it; a tab whose conversation failed starts a new one with it.
- interrupt {cloud_workspace, tab}: Stop the turn a tab's agent is in. The tab stays open.
- answer {cloud_workspace, request, tab, action?, content?, option?}: Answer what a tab's agent asks (read_cloud kind requests): a permission request with option, a question with action (and content, its fields, to accept).
- close_tab {cloud_workspace, tab}: Close a tab: its conversation and agent end; its transcript is kept. The other tabs and the machine carry on.
- rebuild {cloud_workspace, interrupt?}: Replace a Cloud workspace's machine with one set up from its settings as saved: its disk is wiped; its tabs keep their conversations. Refused while a tab's turn runs, unless interrupt.
- retry {cloud_workspace}: Set up a Cloud workspace whose setup failed again (read_cloud kind setup_log says why it failed).

Drive the user's Cloud workspaces in Arugula control, as the user (the owner of this machine): make one, open a tab (an agent on its machine), prompt it and wait for its turn, interrupt it, answer what it asks, close it, rebuild or retry. full, labs true.description:
Build a Doc, a report, plan or write-up longer than a screen, in a block beside your pane that the user (and anyone the session is shared with) watches fill in. Make the outline first with new, so they see every section at once; then fill each section in order and say one sentence about it in the pane. Never write the Doc's files by hand.
- new {sections, title, beside?}: A Doc: a block beside your pane that holds a report, plan or write-up, with its outline (every section's heading and intent) shown at once. Returns the block and the section ids (s1, s2, …); fill them next, in order.
- fill {block, markdown, section}: Write one section of a Doc (its block, the section id, its Markdown): headings, paragraphs, lists, **bold**, *italic*, `code`, links and tables. No HTML. A picture is ![alt](assets/<name>) after doc asset has put it there. A section is at most 64 KB, a Doc 40 sections and 1 MiB; filling a section again replaces it.

Two kinds of fenced block draw as more than code, in the section that talks about them.
A chart: a ```chart fence holding a JSON spec. type is "bar" or "line"; title is optional; x is the key of each row that labels it; y is a key, or a list of up to 4 keys, whose values are numbers (not strings); rows is 1 to 200 objects. A line chart's x must go up: numbers, ISO dates (2026-01-31), or labels listed in order with "order": [...]. For example:
```chart
{"type": "bar", "title": "Sales by month", "x": "month", "y": ["sales"], "rows": [{"month": "Jan", "sales": 12}, {"month": "Feb", "sales": 19}]}
```
A drawing: a ```svg fence holding one <svg> element, with xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" on it and a viewBox. Any text after svg on the fence line is its alt text. It is shown as a picture, so scripts in it don't run. For example:
```svg Idea to app
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 160 40"><rect x="2" y="8" width="60" height="24" fill="#e8f0fe" stroke="#335"/><path d="M62 20 H98" stroke="#335"/><rect x="98" y="8" width="60" height="24" fill="#e6f4ea" stroke="#335"/></svg>
```
Every fence is checked before anything is written: a bad chart or drawing is refused with one line saying what to fix, and the section stays as it was.
- asset {block, name, data?, path?}: Put a picture in a Doc (its block, a name, and one of path or data): a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, at most 2 MB, at most 20 per Doc. path is an absolute path to a file you saved; an agent on a machine of its own sends data (base64) instead. What the bytes are decides the type, so the name has to end in the right extension (.png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif, .webp); an SVG file is refused: draw it with a ```svg fence. Returns assets/<name>; show it in a section with ![what it shows](assets/<name>). Put the asset before the doc fill that names it: a fill naming an asset the Doc doesn't have is refused. Only assets/ images show; an http:// or ../ one is refused. A name already used is replaced. For example: {"kind": "asset", "block": 7, "name": "flow.png", "path": "/tmp/flow.png"}.
- share {block}: Ask the user to share a finished Doc (its block) with a link anyone can open, without an account. A card asks them on the Doc and nothing is published until they tap Share; this returns {status: "waiting"} at once. Call share again on the same block to learn the outcome: shared (with the url, which you can give the user), declined, lapsed (a card nobody answered in a day) or failed (with why). A Doc already shared answers shared. Asking again after a decline raises a new card. Don't ask more than once for a Doc unless the user wants it.

full, labs true.title: Read a Cloud workspace

full, labs true.description:
Drive the user's Cloud workspaces in Arugula control, as the user (the owner of this machine): make one, open a tab (an agent on its machine), prompt it and wait for its turn, interrupt it, answer what it asks, close it, rebuild or retry. The user sees it all on control's page. Changing a Cloud workspace's settings or deleting one is theirs, on that page. A hosted Cloud workspace (hw_…, made with project) is a machine of the project: its tabs are agent blocks on it (claude or codex), by pane number, which the project's people see too; the machine tools reach it with cloud_workspace.
- create {name, apt?, env_vars?, npm?, project?, repositories?, secrets?, setup_script?}: A new Cloud workspace: a machine with these repositories checked out, packages installed and setup script run. It sets up for a few minutes (list kind cloud_workspaces says its step; read_cloud kind setup_log what it printed); a tab opened meanwhile starts once it's ready. Returns its id.
- open_tab {cloud_workspace, agent?, cwd?, model?, prompt?}: A new tab in a Cloud workspace: an agent's conversation on its machine, with a first prompt if given. Returns the tab's id; wait with the tab until idle or needs_input.
- prompt {cloud_workspace, tab, text, timeout?}: Give a tab's agent a prompt and wait for its turn: returns when it ends (done, with the reply), when it asks for someone (needs_input, with its requests: answer one), or still running after timeout, with the offset to wait after. A parked machine wakes for it; a tab whose conversation failed starts a new one with it.
- interrupt {cloud_workspace, tab}: Stop the turn a tab's agent is in. The tab stays open.
- answer {cloud_workspace, request, tab, action?, content?, option?}: Answer what a tab's agent asks (read_cloud kind requests): a permission request with option, a question with action (and content, its fields, to accept).
- close_tab {cloud_workspace, tab}: Close a tab: its conversation and agent end; its transcript is kept. The other tabs and the machine carry on.
- rebuild {cloud_workspace, interrupt?}: Replace a Cloud workspace's machine with one set up from its settings as saved: its disk is wiped; its tabs keep their conversations. Refused while a tab's turn runs, unless interrupt.
- retry {cloud_workspace}: Set up a Cloud workspace whose setup failed again (read_cloud kind setup_log says why it failed).

read, labs true.description:
Read PRs and issues on GitHub repos linked to the user's projects in Arugula control (list kind linked_repos lists them), with no block open: a PR, an issue, a list of them, a PR's checks, or drafts waiting for a person. As the user (the owner of this machine), and only what GitHub lets them read. For a repo that isn't linked, show (kind pr or issue) opens a block instead. Also Arugula's own (native) issues: kind issue with item "#N" (in the current project) or "iss_…", and kind native_issues (with this machine's threads.read grant).
- pr {item}: A pull request: its state, title, author, labels, reviewers, branches, what happened to it (reviews, pushes) and its waiting drafts. Metadata only, no body or comments.
- issue {item, project?}: An issue: its state, title, author, labels, assignees, what happened to it and its waiting drafts. A native issue ("#N" or "iss_…"): it, its timeline and its newest comments.
- items {author?, item_kind?, limit?, project?, q?, repo?, review_requested?, state?}: The PRs and issues of one linked repo, or of a project's linked repos, last updated first; item_kind, state, author, review_requested and q narrow it. Repos the user can't read on GitHub are named as withheld.
- checks {item}: A pull request's checks on its head commit: each one's status and conclusion.
- inbox {done?, limit?}: The user's inbox: PRs and issues on their linked repos that want something of them (a review requested, their checks failed, changes requested, a mention, assigned, merged or ready, a draft waiting), newest first, each with whether they've seen it.
- drafts {item?, project?, state?}: Drafts waiting for a person to send: on a PR or issue, a repo or a project, or the user's own.
- draft {draft}: One draft: what it says and what became of it (waiting, sent with its link, discarded or failed).
- native_issues {assignee?, author?, before?, labels?, limit?, project?, q?, state?}: Arugula's own (native) issues of a project in Arugula control (the current one unless project names it), newest first; state, labels, assignee, author and q (search words) narrow it. issue_write writes to them at once.

read, labs true.description:
Read one of the user's Cloud workspaces in Arugula control (list kind cloud_workspaces lists them, cloud_tabs their tabs): a tab's transcript or what it asks, or its machine's files, diff, git status or setup log. Reading never wakes a parked machine. A hosted Cloud workspace (hw_…) is a machine of a project: its tabs are its agent blocks, by pane number, and reading one wakes it.
- events {cloud_workspace, tab, max_chars?, offset?}: A tab's transcript as text: prompts, the agent's messages, its tool calls and their results, and what it asked. Paged: pass next_offset back as offset.
- requests {cloud_workspace, tab}: What a tab's agent waits on someone for: each permission request with its options, and each question with its fields. cloud {kind: answer} answers one.
- files {cloud_workspace, path?}: A directory on a Cloud workspace's machine: its entries, with type and size.
- file {cloud_workspace, path, max_chars?}: A text file on a Cloud workspace's machine, with secrets redacted.
- diff {cloud_workspace, max_chars?, path?, ref?, staged?}: git diff of the repository holding path on a Cloud workspace's machine (staged, or against ref), with secrets redacted. Without path: its first repository (the summary names the others).
- git_status {cloud_workspace, path?}: git status of the repository holding path on a Cloud workspace's machine: its branch and changed and untracked files. Without path: its first repository (the summary names the others).
- setup_log {cloud_workspace}: What a Cloud workspace's last setup printed, step by step (packages, repositories, setup script): why one failed. Reads while the machine is failed or parked.
